labeledFrom: Read src/App.tsx (router config), listed src/pages/, read server/index.js.
shape: Vite + React SPA with react-router, plus a small Express + Socket.IO server under server/ written in plain JS.
whyThisRepo: Writes pages as `const Index = () => {}; export default Index;`. Under modifier-only export detection every page was `exported: false`, so the repo reported zero UI routes.

uiRoutes.note: src/pages/ holds exactly these two files and App.tsx declares exactly two <Route> elements.

declaredPaths.note: App.tsx:14-15. The catch-all is written `path="*"`; we normalise it to a root-relative `/*`.

httpRoutes.note: server/index.js:22 `app.get('/health', ...)`. This is a .js file — it is only reachable because the parser accepts .js, which `filterByLanguage(index,'typescript')` does not.

socketEvents.note: server/src/handlers.js registers eleven socket.on events inside io.on('connection'). These are the app's real interaction surface — the only HTTP route is a health check, so before socket detection this repo produced a single workflow and looked inert.

knownGaps: Server-to-client emits (`io.to(room).emit('turn-started', …)`, 34 of them in GameRoom.js) are the other half of the realtime protocol and are not modeled. They are outputs rather than entrypoints, so they belong with side-effect/response classification rather than with entrypoint detection.
